newsitem.title: QATAR: Qatar's second LNG venture starts drilling.
newsitem.headline: Qatar's second LNG venture starts drilling.

text.p: Qatar's Ras Laffan Liquefied Natural Gas Company (Rasgas) said on Sunday it has started drilling for gas for its first production unit to supply LNG to South Korea.
"Another milestone has been accomplished in Rasgas production process as the drilling task force commenced drilling at two locations for the first train," said a press release issued by the company.
The first jack-up rig, Hakuryu 8, began drilling at wellhead platform 2 on April 3 and the second rig, Ensco 96, at platform 1 on April 4, said the statement.
"We are currently drilling a 36-inch hole to set 30 inches casing at an approximate 600 feet depth," it said.

"The drilling operations are planned to go on for 540 days," said a Rasgas official. He said 15 wells will be drilled to produce around five million tonnes of LNG from two "trains" of 2.6 million tonne capacity each.
"We will drill two wells this year, eight next year and the remaining five in the third quarter of 1999," he said.
Rasgas is one of Qatar's three multibillion-dollar gas export projects to tap reserves in North Field, the world's largest single concentration of gas.
The first project, Qatar Liquefied Gas Company (Qatargas) is onstream with a commitment to supply six million tonnes a year of LNG to the Japanese market for 25 years.
Rasgas has signed an agreement to export 4.8 million tonnes of gas annually for 25 years to Seoul's Korea Gas Corporation (Kogas) from mid-1999.

The company is 63 percent owned by the state's Qatar General Petroleum Corporation, 25 percent by U.S. Mobil Corp, four percent by Itochu, three percent by Nissho and five an undisclosed South Korean entity of five percent, designated by Kogas.
A third project, Qatar-Enron LNG Marketing Company, is planned.
